issues.legal_issue: An accused who initiates an armed attack cannot rely on private defence against the response to that attack when the alleged victim is found to have been unarmed.
material_facts: The accused came armed to the complainant party’s home, abused and challenged its occupants, and initiated the confrontation.
The deceased was attacked at the start of the ensuing fight; the courts rejected the claim that he had first attacked an accused and found him unarmed.
The injured son participated in the fight after his father had been attacked, but the accused who inflicted his grievous injury had been part of the aggressing group.
issues.conclusion: The plea of private defence was unavailable to the accused who attacked the deceased and to the accused who inflicted the grievous injury on the deceased’s son.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the law of private defence under the Indian Penal Code to the facts found by the courts below. Since the accused were the aggressors and the deceased’s alleged prior attack was disbelieved, neither private defence nor the question of exceeding that right arose. The Court relied on the factual reasons given by the High Court and cited no earlier case for this issue.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal by an accused challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.accused_initiated_armed_confrontation: The accused arrived armed and initiated the confrontation that led to the violence.
predicates.alleged_victim_did_not_first_attack: The court found that the alleged victim did not first attack the accused.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a conviction after initiating an armed confrontation and the court finds that the alleged victim did not attack first, the rule states that private defence is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: The exception for culpable homicide committed in a sudden fight does not apply when armed accused prepare for a fight, provoke the confrontation, and take undue advantage of an unarmed victim.
material_facts: The accused went armed to the complainant party’s home, provoked the occupants, and initiated the confrontation.
A mutual fight followed, but the deceased was unarmed and was attacked at the outset with deadly blows.
The deceased was selected as a target despite being unarmed.
issues.conclusion: Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC did not apply, and the offence could not be reduced to culpable homicide on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC applies where culpable homicide is committed without premeditation in a sudden fight, in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel, and without the offender taking undue advantage or acting cruelly or unusually. Its explanation makes it immaterial which party provoked the quarrel or committed the first assault. The Court held that a mutual fight alone is not a sudden fight preceded by a sudden quarrel, and that the accused had taken undue advantage.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_murder_convictio: The proceeding is an accused’s appeal against a murder conviction.
predicates.accused_prepared_for_fight: The accused arrived armed and prepared to fight.
predicates.accused_provoked_confrontation: The accused provoked the confrontation that led to the fight.
predicates.unarmed_victim_targeted: The accused attacked a victim who was unarmed.
predicates.accused_took_undue_advantage: The accused used the victim’s unarmed condition to attack him in a way that took undue advantage.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a murder conviction after arriving prepared for a fight, provoking the confrontation, targeting an unarmed victim, and taking undue advantage, the rule states that the sudden-fight exception is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: Common intention to cause bodily injuries likely to cause death, formed during an attack, supports culpable homicide liability but does not establish murder where an intention to kill or inflict ordinarily fatal injuries is not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
material_facts: Three accused acted together in attacking the deceased, who had intervened in the confrontation.
The deceased suffered multiple head injuries, including two fatal injuries, but the evidence did not establish which accused inflicted which injuries.

The court found that the common intention to cause bodily injuries developed at the scene, but that the accused had not formed a common intention to kill the deceased or inflict injuries ordinarily sufficient to cause death.
issues.conclusion: The murder convictions of the three accused under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC were set aside and replaced with convictions for culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304 Part I read with Section 34 IPC.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 IPC requires a common intention and participation in the criminal act. A pre-arranged plan and meeting of minds are required, although the plan may develop at the scene; the common intention must precede the act constituting the offence. It may be inferred from conduct showing unity of purpose, the part played by the accused, the injuries inflicted, and other relevant circumstances. The Court relied on Krishna v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1963 SC 1413, and Ramashish Yadav v. State of Bihar, [1999] 8 SCC 555. Applying Sections 302 and 304 Part I IPC, the Court found a common intention to cause injuries likely to cause death, but reasonable doubt as to a common intention to kill or inflict injuries ordinarily sufficient to cause death.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_murder_convictio: The proceeding is an accused’s appeal against a murder conviction.
predicates.accused_acted_in_concert: The accused participated together in the attack on the victim.
predicates.common_intention_to_cause_likely_fatal_i: Before inflicting the relevant injuries, the accused formed a common intention to cause bodily injuries likely to cause death, even if that intention arose during the incident.
predicates.reasonable_doubt_about_intention_to_kill: The evidence leaves reasonable doubt that the accused shared an intention to kill or to inflict injuries ordinarily sufficient to cause death.

issues.definition: When accused appealing murder convictions acted together after forming a common intention to cause likely fatal injuries, but the evidence leaves reasonable doubt about an intention to kill, the rule states that the murder convictions are replaced with culpable homicide convictions.

issues.legal_issue: Participation in a mutual fight does not by itself make every member of an unlawful assembly constructively liable for another member’s acts when the assembly did not share the relevant common object, although rioting liability may remain established.
material_facts: The complainant appealed the High Court’s refusal to apply Section 149 IPC and its acquittal of some accused.
The High Court found that a mutual fight occurred and held that accused other than the three principal attackers were responsible only for their individual acts.

The Supreme Court found that the three principal attackers were members of an unlawful assembly of at least five persons whose common object fell within Section 141(iii), but whose common object was not to kill or hurt the deceased.
The three principal attackers were found to have acted together in attacking the deceased.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not restore constructive liability under Section 149 for the other accused and disposed of the complainant’s appeal in accordance with its judgment on the accused’s appeal. It upheld the three principal attackers’ convictions under Section 148 IPC.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 141 and 149 IPC govern unlawful assembly and constructive liability for offences committed in prosecution of an assembly’s common object or those members knew to be likely. The Court found an unlawful assembly within Section 141(iii), but distinguished that common object from an intention to kill or hurt the deceased. It held the other accused responsible for their individual acts in the circumstances of the mutual fight. The three principal attackers’ participation in rioting was punishable under Section 148 IPC. No earlier case was cited for this issue.

predicates.complainant_appeal_challenges_constructi: The proceeding is an appeal by a complainant challenging the refusal to impose collective criminal liability on other participants.
predicates.mutual_fight_occurred: The court found that opposing groups engaged in a mutual fight.
predicates.assembly_lacked_relevant_common_object: The assembly did not share a common object to commit the offence for which collective liability is sought.
predicates.participants_committed_distinct_individu: The participants other than the principal attackers were found responsible for their own individual acts.

issues.definition: When a complainant appeals the refusal to impose collective liability, but the court finds a mutual fight, no relevant common object, and distinct individual acts by other participants, the rule states that constructive liability is not extended to those participants.

issues.legal_issue: A grievous injury inflicted with a sharp weapon is sufficient to sustain a conviction where direct eyewitness evidence identifies the assailant and medical evidence confirms the injury’s nature.
material_facts: An eyewitness gave clear and categorical evidence that the accused attacked the deceased’s son.
The initial report also alleged that the accused participated in the attack.
Medical evidence established that the victim’s thumb injury was grievous and had been inflicted with a sharp weapon.
The victim was armed and participated in the fight after his father was attacked.
issues.conclusion: The conviction under Section 326 IPC was upheld; the victim’s participation in the fight did not establish a right of private defence for the accused.
issues.legal_principle: Section 326 IPC applies to voluntarily causing grievous hurt by a dangerous weapon or means. The Court relied on the eyewitness evidence, its corroboration by the initial report, and the medical evidence establishing a grievous sharp-weapon injury. It rejected private defence for the reasons applicable to the aggressors in the same confrontation.

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_grievous_hurt_co: The proceeding is an accused’s appeal against a conviction for grievous hurt.
predicates.eyewitness_identified_assailant: An eyewitness clearly identified the accused as the person who inflicted the injury.
predicates.medical_evidence_confirmed_grievous_shar: Medical evidence confirmed that the victim suffered grievous hurt caused by a sharp weapon.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals a grievous-hurt conviction and an eyewitness identifies the assailant while medical evidence confirms a grievous sharp-weapon injury, the rule states that the conviction is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A sentence may be adjusted to reflect the circumstances of the offence and the imprisonment already undergone, while ordering the resulting fine or compensation as part of the disposition.
material_facts: The three principal attackers had already undergone about eight years of imprisonment when the Court considered their sentences for culpable homicide and rioting.
The accused convicted of grievous hurt had already undergone about eight months of imprisonment.
The Court considered the facts and circumstances of the case and directed that the imprisonment already undergone by the appellants be set off against their sentences.
issues.conclusion: The three principal attackers were sentenced to eight years’ rigorous imprisonment for the main offence, with an enhanced fine, and one year’s rigorous imprisonment for rioting, with the sentences concurrent. The grievous-hurt offender’s sentence was reduced to two years’ rigorous imprisonment and the fine was enhanced to be paid to the injured person as compensation. Time already served was to be set off.
issues.legal_principle: The Court exercised its sentencing discretion in light of the facts and circumstances of the case and the periods of imprisonment already undergone. It cited no separate sentencing provision or earlier case as the basis for these adjustments.

predicates.criminal_appeal_involves_sentence_review: The proceeding is a criminal appeal in which the court reviews the sentence.
predicates.court_considers_case_circumstances: The court considers the circumstances of the offence and the offender when determining the sentence.
predicates.imprisonment_already_undergone: The offender has already undergone a material period of imprisonment before the sentence is reviewed.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal involves sentence review, the court considers the case circumstances and imprisonment already undergone, and the rule states that the sentence is adjusted to account for those considerations.
